clue.text: Immodest acts online had to lead to tears

parts.note: E- is the usual short prefix for electronic or online, as in email
had to and got to are the same; got stands for had here
tears as a verb, rips apart

explanation.surface: Someone shows off on the internet and ends up crying about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lead to' only joins the pieces in order; read 'tears' as rips, not weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-indulgent displays of vanity are bouts of boastful self-promotion, so 'immodest acts' describes them.

clue.text: Somebody's about, it's horrible — stop it!

indicators.note: about says the word for somebody is turned round

parts.note: one is an indefinite somebody, as in 'one does one's best'
ugh is the exclamation of disgust at something horrible

explanation.surface: Someone is hanging around, it is awful, and the speaker begs for it to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'that will do!' is an order to stop, said when one has had sufficient.

clue.text: Badly coiffured politician flipped two days in — bodyguard screened

indicators.note: in says the days are placed inside the reversed nickname
flipped means the nickname is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: Boris Johnson, known for his unruly hair, is nicknamed BoJo
D is the abbreviation for day, so two days give D twice

explanation.surface: A messy-haired politician did a two-day U-turn while his minder stayed out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screened' looks like hidden but means shown on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The hat-throwing henchman of Goldfinger in the Bond film is a bodyguard seen on the cinema screen.

clue.text: Eager to go after group of artists

parts.note: RA stands for the Royal Academy of Arts, or a Royal Academician, artists
a ring is a group, as of conspirators or dealers

explanation.surface: A painter is keen to leave once the art collective has had its turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' belongs to the definition, from the phrase 'raring to go'; 'after' and 'of' just join.
explanation.definitionFit: To be keen to start, impatient for action, is the meaning of the idiom with these words.

clue.text: Old pile condemned — at first they live inside like pigs

indicators.note: inside says these letters go within the rearranged pile
a condemned building is to be knocked down, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt
at first takes only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to live is to be, exist

explanation.surface: A condemned old building where the residents live like pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like pigs' reads as a slur on the residents but defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs have big round bellies, so to be paunchy-bodied is to be like a pig.

clue.text: Order a wife from the east — here's the money

indicators.note: in an across clue reading from the east means going right to left, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: to order someone is to tell them to do something

explanation.surface: A man arranges a mail-order bride from Asia and asks where the payment is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket case for banknotes and cards is where one's cash is kept, hence the playful description.

clue.text: End up gutted, after "pretend" gangster got off

indicators.note: after says the rest comes below the gangster in this down entry

parts.note: Ali G is the fake gangster character played by Sacha Baron Cohen

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards
gutted says the middle letter is removed from the word for end

parts.note: death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A wannabe gangster comes to a miserable end, then escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like dismay but takes the A out of DEATH, giving DETH; 'up' turns it to HTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to step down from a vehicle, so having done so means having got off.

clue.text: Working girl cycling round picks up current lover

indicators.note: in a down entry picking up means the round letter carries the current symbol above it
cycling means the halves of the word rotate round, the back letters coming first

parts.note: working girl is a euphemism for a prostitute, a harlot
I is the symbol for electric current
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A prostitute on a bicycle picks up a new boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' swaps the two halves of the working girl; 'picks up' places the current symbol on top of the round letter in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, from a character in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, so a womanising lover.

clue.text: Cross after very cunning set-up — language!

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the letters go upwards, read backwards

parts.note: art is cunning or skill
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Someone is angry after a crafty scheme, and swears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, and 'language!' like swearing; Cross is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross or travel across an area.

clue.text: Make a speech about British — some of the French hard to persuade

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speech-making word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
du is French for 'some of the' (masculine), as in du pain

explanation.surface: A speaker addresses Britons and some French people who will not be easily won over.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly unyielding, a person whom argument does not move.

clue.text: As is traditional, provides instruments

indicators.note: provides says the phrase before it supplies the answer from within its letters

explanation.surface: As custom dictates, someone supplies the musical instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'As' through 'is' into 'traditional'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sistra are ancient Egyptian rattles, metal frames with jingling rods shaken in worship, so they are musical instruments.

clue.text: Good — well-developed and sensible

parts.note: a rounded character or education is fully and well developed

explanation.surface: A list of praise for a person: decent, mature and level-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounded person is level-headed and practical, which is to be sensible.

clue.text: Epithet "whale" also fitted subject of this enquiry

definitions.text: Epithet "whale" also fitted subject of this enquiry

indicators.note: fitted is read as rearranged, the letters fitted together anew

explanation.surface: Calling someone a whale suits the person this question is about.
explanation.walkthrough: The football chant asks this of a heavy player; the clue's insult would fit that same target, so the whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The terrace chant mocks an overweight footballer, the very person who might also be called a whale.

clue.text: Unhappy naked? Is it time you went on it?

definitions.text: Unhappy naked? Is it time you went on it?

indicators.note: unhappy letters are disturbed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes their body undressed and wonders about starting a slimming regime.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a question to someone unhappy at their naked shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The low-carbohydrate slimming plan devised by Dr Robert Atkins is what someone unhappy with their figure might start.

clue.text: See 12
Prepared to do business, spoke more freely

definitions.meaning: a shop that has started trading for the day has unlocked its doors
to become more communicative, sharing feelings

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who was ready to trade became more talkative.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a shop starting trade and a person confiding are said to have done this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Figure childishly drawn — staff supporting criticism

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: stick is informal British for criticism, as in 'giving someone stick'
to staff is to man, to provide workers

explanation.surface: A child's drawing of a figure holding a stick, used against critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like a stick but is the verb to man.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple figure of lines and a circle head is what children draw for a person.

clue.text: Stagger out of university, sort of

parts.note: Aston University is in Birmingham, England
-ish means sort of, somewhat

explanation.surface: Someone sort of lurches out of a university building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' reads as reeling but means amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to amaze them greatly, a synonym.

clue.text: Tarts here — naughty peer's not against a visit

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving letters, so the words are rearranged
not says the letter for against is dropped from the words beside it

parts.note: V, for versus, is the usual abbreviation for against

explanation.surface: A disreputable lord's visit to some ladies of the night is not opposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tarts' suggests prostitutes and 'naughty peer' plays along; the tarts are pastries.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry shop is where fruit tarts and other cakes are sold, so tarts are found here.

clue.text: Neither partner's masculine — largely typical

parts.note: nor partners neither in the pair 'neither ... nor'

indicators.note: largely says most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: masculine means male

explanation.surface: In this couple neither is manly, which is mostly how things are.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal and typical both mean usual, conforming to the standard.

clue.text: Girl is turning over to get brown

indicators.note: turning over says the words are turned upside down in this down entry, read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl turns over in the sun to get a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment, a yellowish or reddish brown colour.

clue.text: Intuitive knowledge upset number one son

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a number is a song, a musical item
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A parent's instinct is upset by their eldest son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a figure but is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is spiritual knowledge grasped directly by insight rather than reasoning.

clue.text: On return, look round house for snacks

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes around the other piece
on return says the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: to scan is to look over something

explanation.surface: Coming back, someone looks around the house for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortilla chips with toppings are a popular Mexican nibble, a kind of snack.

clue.text: Schoolboy boxing southern European

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the schoolboy goes around the other letter

parts.note: a pupil at Eton College, the English public school, is an Etonian

explanation.surface: A schoolboy takes up boxing against a southern European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Estonia, a Baltic state, is a European.

clue.text: Idiot! Lad I'm with is not all there

indicators.note: not all there says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone apologises that the boy accompanying them is a bit simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all there' reads as a jibe about the lad but says only part of the words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is a stupid person, a synonym for idiot.

clue.text: Food's left in a different place, causing complaints

indicators.note: in a different place says one letter is moved to another position in the word

parts.note: aliments are foods, nourishment

explanation.surface: Food was left out somewhere it should not be, and people got ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the L of ALIMENTS to second place gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints in the medical sense are illnesses or disorders, which is what ailments are.

clue.text: Hard-hitting article ignored by 4

indicators.note: ignored by says the article is left out of the word for the cross-referenced clue

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer at 4 down, which means having a big belly, as does paunchy
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A forceful piece of writing that a pot-bellied reader ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Punchy means forceful and effective, as a hard-hitting speech or article is.

clue.text: Isn't a fashion having ringmaster in Dolce & Gabbana?

indicators.note: having means holding, so the rearranged letters hold the boxer inside
to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was a master of the boxing ring

explanation.surface: A question about whether a fashion house with a circus ringmaster is really fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringmaster' suggests the circus but is the boxer Ali. The question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana, the designers, are two people from Italy, examples of the nationality.
